contentBlocks.text: You can break numbers into tens and ones. Today: use that skill to quickly compare which of two numbers is bigger.

To compare two-digit numbers, look at the tens digit first — more tens always means a bigger number. For example, comparing 34 and 29: 34 has 3 tens, 29 has 2 tens, so 34 is bigger, even though 9 (in the ones place) looks like a big digit. Only if the tens digits are equal do you compare the ones digit. Compare 52 and 58: both have 5 tens, so compare ones — 8 is more than 2, so 58 is bigger. Compare 41 and 14, explaining which is bigger and why.
You now have a real strategy for comparing two-digit numbers — check tens first, then ones only if needed! Tomorrow we'll use tens and ones to add numbers.

objectives: Compare two two-digit numbers by comparing tens digits first, then ones digits if needed
Explain why the tens digit matters more than the ones digit when comparing
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's tens/ones breakdown.
2. Introduce the tens-first comparison strategy using 34 vs. 29.
3. Practice a same-tens comparison (52 vs. 58).
4. Have the child compare 41 and 14 independently, explaining their reasoning.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Close by comparing two numbers the child picks themselves.
differentiationTips: Struggling: physically bundle both numbers into tens and ones objects before comparing, rather than working from written digits alone
Ready for more: ask the child to find a number between two given numbers (e.g., between 34 and 41)
The 41-vs-14 example is deliberately chosen — same digits, different order, very different values, a common early misconception worth addressing directly
teacherGuide.answerKey: 41 is bigger than 14, because 41 has 4 tens while 14 has only 1 ten — even though both numbers use the same two digits.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 1 standard 1.NBT.3: comparing two two-digit numbers based on the meanings of the tens and ones digits, applying yesterday's place-value breakdown skill.
